pairs.question: Quis causas reddere possit?
pairs.answer: Sic iussit natura parens discurrere Nilum, sic opus est mundo.
pairs.derivation: Within Acoreus' discourse on the Nile, the speaker poses a rhetorical question (who could give the causes of the flooding?) and immediately answers it himself: nature the parent ordered the Nile to flow thus, and thus the world requires it. Answer window ends at the full stop after 'mundo'; what follows ('Zephyros quoque uana uetustas...') turns to refuting the wind-theory and no longer answers this question.
